result.reason: Both items are the Mishnah text that opens the final section of the tractate, covering the rules of wailing and clapping on Chol HaMoed, Rosh Chodesh, Hanukkah, Purim, and after burial — precisely what candidate 14 ('Women Wailing Rules') describes in its prose.

Both items — the definition of wailing/lament and the concluding forward-looking verse about death being swallowed forever — are explicitly discussed in the 'Mourning Types' prose, which covers the Mishnah's definitions of inuy, kina, and the closing Isaiah verse.

All six items — Rav's wailing phrase, Rava's multiple Shekhantziv women's sayings, and Rabbi Meir's baraita on laying death to heart — are explicitly discussed together in the 'Shnitziv Wailing' section prose, which covers exactly this sequence of content.

Both items describe the opening of the consolation visit to Rabbi Yishmael — the elders' arrival, Rabbi Tarfon's instructions, Rabbi Akiva's deferral, and Rabbi Yishmael's self-deprecating opening remarks — which is precisely what the 'Yishmael Consoled' prose section describes.

All 7 items are the continuous baraita of kal vachomer proofs by Rabbi Tarfon, Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, and Rabbi Akiva regarding the sons of Rabbi Yishmael, which is precisely what candidate 0's prose describes in detail.
All three items form a continuous discussion of resolving contradictory verses about dying 'in peace' for Zedekiah and Josiah, which is precisely what the 'Death Verses Resolved' prose describes.
The passage discusses the ruling that consolers must wait for the mourner to speak first, which is exactly what the 'Consoler Etiquette' section's prose addresses in detail.
All five items discuss the same topic — who sits at the head of the table (mourner, then groom, then priest) — which is precisely what the 'Mourner Head Seat' prose describes in detail.
Both items together form Rabbi Ḥanina's and Rabbi Yoḥanan's statements about the difficulty of the soul's departure, which is precisely what the 'Soul Struggle' prose describes.

All three items discuss the same teaching about parting blessings for the dead vs. the living (leich b'shalom vs. leich l'shalom), which is precisely what the 'Parting Blessings' prose section discusses in detail, including the same proofs from Abraham, David/Absalom, and Jethro/Moses.
